scope: Speech is shorter and more exact on every screen. Keys keep your place, and web pages read like a screen reader would read them.

topics.title: Web pages
details: Tab now stops on tabs, switches and spin buttons. F finds switches and spin buttons too.
Enter picks a tab. Enter or Space turns a switch on or off.
Enter on a spin button lets the arrows change it.
A field says what is in it. It also says when the site marks it wrong, and reads the site's hint.
T says how many rows and columns a table has.
You hear Top of page or Bottom of page at the ends of a page.

topics.title: New ways to say things
details: Say where am I in Help to hear where you are.
Say what mode am I in, or switch to dictation only, from any screen.
On Calendar, say schedule lunch with Bob tomorrow at noon.
In File manager, say what is selected.
In email, say read message fifteen, or what folder am I in.

topics.title: Startup, sleep and Help
details: If you wake up at a yes or no question, the question is asked again.
With the microphone off, sleep tells you to press Control+F12 to wake up.
Canceled is now said with where you are, so you hear it.
Leaving Help says Help closed.
Moving in Help says only the item. The hint is said once.
Mode and version questions work in Help.
Saying no to an update while asleep takes you back to your screen.
The transcript notice at startup says to wake Companion first.
The tutorial names all twelve courses, and its lists sound like the rest of the app.

topics.title: Email
details: Subjects end with one period. A blank subject says No subject.
Canceling a reply takes you back to the message you were reading.
Closing a saved draft says it is still saved.
Delete in Trash and moving to the same folder now say nothing changed.
Marking messages says the same words by key and by voice.
An empty folder gives the same answer to every key.
Escape from attachments says the message you are on.
Spoken numbers up to one hundred work.

topics.title: Calendar and Contacts
details: If an event or contact was removed somewhere else, the list is read again.
Where am I and Repeat keep your place.
Both screens know next item, top of list and bottom of list.
Y and N no longer close the Calendar lists.
Asking what is on your calendar names a calendar that cannot be read.
Email John says why if Thunderbird cannot give its contacts.

topics.title: Documents and files
details: Reading a paragraph or line no longer moves your place.
Deleting a word or sentence leaves no extra spaces.
Messages no longer end with two periods.
Format changes are said in plain words, such as Italic or Heading 2.
Make it quick, and other sentences that start with make it, are written.
Redo goes to the paragraph it changes.
Find in the Document reader works with the period speech adds.
File manager says 1 item, not 1 items.
If Desktop is missing, Save As suggests Documents.

topics.title: Web
details: Controls are said in the same words on the page and with quick keys.
Unnamed controls no longer say their type twice.
Saving a favorite by voice never replaces another favorite.
List form fields and show fields open the fields list.

topics.title: Media
details: Page Down and Page Up move ten videos on YouTube.
Space on the player controls keeps you on the control you chose.
Keys in an empty list say the list is empty.
If YouTube does not send more videos, you hear why and what to do.
A podcast episode that is slow to start still opens the player controls.
End in the Media player tells you how to reach the player menu.
